generatedProse.concept-context: In the School of Sport, this means bringing the three ideas to every search, whether the topic is coaching, physiology or sport management. You decide what you are looking for, choose keywords such as 'training', 'endurance' and 'recovery', then search and weigh what comes back. A coaching search and a lab-report search use the same practice. Making this your normal way of searching is what steadily improves the sources you find.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport students each need sources for a report on training. Tom types the whole question into a search box and uses the first result, with no plan and no second look. Amara uses the whole practice instead: she sets an objective, picks keywords with a synonym, searches, then weighs which sources are suitable. Both knew the topic, but Amara found clearer, more trustworthy sources, because her search used every part of the practice.
generatedProse.summary: Academic searching in the School of Sport is most useful when you treat it as one practice, not three separate ideas. You bring the same moves to every search: know what you are looking for, plan, choose keywords, then search and weigh what you find. Making this your normal way of searching is what steadily improves the sources behind your sport work.

check.body: A student decides what they are looking for, chooses keywords with a synonym, searches, and weighs the sources before using them. What does this show?

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That they are using the whole searching practice: the three ideas working together, from deciding what they want to weighing what they find.
_items.feedback: Yes. Every idea is there, working together as one practice.

_items.text: That they are doing more than any search really needs.
_items.feedback: No. Each part does a different job, and together they make the search stronger.

_items.text: That only the keywords really matter in a search.
_items.feedback: Not so. Keywords are one part of the practice, not the whole of it.

_items.text: That weighing the sources is the same as planning the search.
_items.feedback: They are different parts: planning comes first, and weighing the sources comes later.
